title: area measurement of squares and rectangles

lesson.title: How Big Is My Rectangle? Finding Area!

steps.say: Imagine you and your family are putting new tiles on the floor of your bedroom in Vancouver. The store asks a question: how many square metres of tile do you need? That is a question about area. Area means how much flat space is inside a shape, and we measure it by counting little squares that cover it.

visual.caption: A bedroom floor, four metres long and three metres wide

steps.say: Let's cover that floor with tiles that are one metre by one metre. Look, we can fit four tiles across each row, and we have three rows going down. Count them all up with me: four, eight, twelve. Twelve square tiles cover the whole floor.

visual.caption: Three rows of four tiles — twelve square metres in all

steps.say: Counting one by one takes a long time, so here is the shortcut. Three rows with four tiles in each row is just three times four, which is twelve. So the area of a rectangle is length times width. We write the answer as twelve square metres, because we counted squares.

visual.caption: Three groups of four make twelve

steps.say: Now let's try one together. Your family buys a rectangular picnic blanket for Stanley Park. It is seven metres long and two metres wide. Seven times two is fourteen. So the blanket covers fourteen square metres of grass.

visual.caption: A picnic blanket, seven metres by two metres

steps.say: A square is just a special rectangle where all four sides are the same length. Here is a square garden box that is five metres on every side. Length times width is five times five, which is twenty-five. So its area is twenty-five square metres.

visual.caption: A square garden box, five metres on each side

steps.say: Here is a slightly harder one. You are making a poster for your classroom that is twelve centimetres long and eight centimetres wide. Twelve times eight is ninety-six. So your poster covers ninety-six square centimetres. Notice that when we measure in centimetres, the area is in square centimetres.

visual.caption: Twelve times eight: ten times eight is eighty, plus two times eight is sixteen, so ninety-six

steps.say: One last thing to remember. Perimeter is the walk around the edge, but area is the space inside. For that poster, the perimeter would be twelve plus eight plus twelve plus eight, which is forty centimetres of ribbon around the edge. But the area, the paper inside, is ninety-six square centimetres. Different jobs, different measurements!

visual.caption: Edge is perimeter, forty centimetres; inside is area, ninety-six square centimetres

steps.say: So whenever someone asks how much space is inside a rectangle or a square, you already know what to do: multiply the two sides, and say your answer in square units.

lesson.answer: Area of a rectangle or square equals length times width — and the answer is always in square units.

practice.question: Your family is putting new grass in a rectangular back yard in Kelowna. The yard is 9 metres long and 6 metres wide. What is the area of the yard? If grass costs 5 dollars for every square metre, how much will it cost in total?
practice.answer: The area is 9 × 6 = 54 square metres. The cost is 54 × $5 = $270.
